text: What is a meteorite?
choices: A rock that reaches a planet's surface from space
A cloud of gas around a star

A stony-iron meteorite contains substantial amounts of what combination?
What is a bolide?
choices: A meteor producing an exceptionally bright fireball
A crater rim made of ejecta

text: Which material commonly makes up ordinary chondrites?
What are chondrules?
choices: Small rounded silicate grains formed as molten droplets
Metal veins in an iron meteorite

text: Which meteorite group is especially rich in carbon and volatile compounds?
The Canyon Diablo meteorites are associated with which crater?
Where is Meteor Crater located?
What is the main source of most meteorites collected on Earth?

What does a meteorite's fusion crust indicate?

What is a meteorite fall?

A meteor shower seen from Earth

text: What is a meteorite find?
choices: A meteorite discovered without observing its fall
A sample collected on an asteroid

text: Which property is commonly measured when classifying an iron meteorite?
choices: Its nickel content and structural pattern

text: What is the radiant of a meteor shower?
choices: The apparent point from which meteors seem to travel
The brightest point of a crater
The location of a meteorite laboratory
The center of an impact basin

text: The Perseids are produced mainly by debris from which object?
What does a meteorite's hand specimen density help distinguish?
choices: Metal-rich material from porous silicate material

text: Which meteorite type is generally differentiated rather than primitive?
Why are freshly fallen meteorites often curated quickly?
choices: To limit terrestrial weathering and contamination

text: What is the primary distinction between a meteoroid and a meteorite?
choices: A meteoroid is in space; a meteorite has reached the ground
A meteoroid is metallic; a meteorite is always stony
A meteoroid orbits Earth; a meteorite orbits the Sun
A meteoroid is visible; a meteorite is never visible

text: Which mineral is a common major phase in many stony meteorites?
What does an H chondrite's letter generally indicate?
choices: A high abundance of water ice

text: What is a regmaglypt?
choices: A thumbprint-like depression on a meteorite surface
A mineral inclusion in lunar rock

text: Which isotope system is commonly used for absolute dating of very old meteorites?
What does a meteorite's cosmic-ray exposure age estimate?
choices: How long it traveled as a small body in space
How long it sat in a museum

text: Which meteorite is widely interpreted as originating from Mars?
How were Martian meteorites identified as Martian?
choices: Their trapped gases match the Martian atmosphere
They are all made of iron

text: What is an impact crater?
choices: A depression formed by a high-speed collision
A valley carved only by glaciers
A volcanic cone filled with ash

text: Which feature is characteristic of a complex impact crater?
choices: A central uplift and terraced walls
A lava fountain at its center
A perfectly flat floor without ejecta

text: What is ejecta?
choices: Material thrown outward during an impact
Dust emitted by a comet's nucleus

text: Which crater is commonly linked to the end-Cretaceous mass extinction?
Chicxulub crater is buried beneath which region?
choices: The Yucatán Peninsula and Gulf of Mexico

text: What is shatter cone evidence of?
Which mineral can record high-pressure shock metamorphism?
Planar deformation features in quartz are important because they are?
choices: Diagnostic microscopic evidence of impact shock
A type of volcanic gas bubble

text: What is impact melt?
choices: Rock melted by the energy of an impact

text: Which crater is the largest confirmed impact structure on Earth?
Vredefort impact structure is located in which country?
What is a tektite?
choices: Natural glass formed from terrestrial material during an impact
A volcanic crystal from a lava tube

text: Australasian tektites are best interpreted as ejecta from what?
What does an impactor's kinetic energy depend on most directly?
choices: Its mass and the square of its velocity

text: Why do larger impactors often create more complex craters?
choices: Their energy causes collapse and central uplift
They travel more slowly through space

text: Which observation can help identify an impact crater when erosion has obscured its rim?
choices: A circular gravity or magnetic anomaly with shock evidence
A straight river valley with no deformation

text: What is a peak ring?
choices: An inner ring of uplifted rock in a large complex crater
A ring of volcanic ash around a cone
A belt of asteroids around Jupiter

text: Which process can preserve impact craters especially well on the Moon?
choices: The lack of wind and liquid-water erosion

text: Why are lunar craters useful for relative chronology?
choices: Older surfaces generally have more accumulated craters
All craters form at the same known rate

text: What is crater saturation?
choices: A surface state where new craters tend to erase old ones
Complete flooding of a crater by lava

text: Which method can reveal an impactor's extraterrestrial contribution in a sediment layer?
choices: Measuring an anomalous abundance of platinum-group elements

text: Why is iridium often examined in studies of the K–Pg boundary?
choices: Its abundance can indicate an asteroid-derived component
It is the main mineral in limestone
It forms only in Earth's core

text: What does a meteorite's petrologic type primarily describe?
choices: Its degree of thermal and aqueous alteration

text: In chondrite classification, what does the petrologic type 3 generally signify?
choices: A sample formed on Earth's seafloor

text: What is oxygen-isotope analysis used for in meteorite research?
choices: Tracing genetic relationships among planetary materials

text: Why are calcium-aluminum-rich inclusions important?
choices: They are among the oldest solids formed in the Solar System
They are products of modern terrestrial weathering
They form only in impact craters

text: What is an achondrite's defining broad characteristic?
choices: It lacks chondrules and commonly records igneous differentiation
It consists entirely of unaltered chondrules
It is always composed of iron metal
It must come from a comet

text: HED meteorites are commonly linked to which asteroid?
What is a pallasite?
choices: A stony-iron meteorite with olivine crystals in metal
A glassy tektite from a crater

text: What does Widmanstätten structure reveal about many iron meteorites?
choices: Very slow cooling in a differentiated metallic core
Melting by a recent volcanic eruption

text: Why is the Widmanstätten pattern usually not reproduced in terrestrial iron?
choices: Earth's iron alloys rarely cool slowly enough to form it
It forms only in meteorite craters

text: What is shock darkening in a meteorite?
choices: Optical darkening caused by shock-driven fracturing and metal redistribution
Darkening from exposure to sunlight alone
A black coating applied during curation
A color found only in carbonaceous chondrites

text: Which technique can map elemental distributions across a meteorite thin section?
What does a cosmic-ray exposure age not directly measure?
choices: The absolute age of the meteorite's parent body
Time spent exposed as a small body in space

text: Why can noble gases date cosmic-ray exposure?
choices: Cosmic rays produce measurable isotopes in minerals
Noble gases crystallize at crater rims
They are absent from all terrestrial rocks
They directly record an eyewitness fall

text: What is the Yarkovsky effect?
choices: A small thermal recoil force that changes an asteroid's orbit
A type of iron meteorite structure
A method for polishing thin sections

text: Why is the Yarkovsky effect relevant to planetary defense?
choices: It can alter the long-term trajectory of potentially hazardous asteroids
It makes impact craters easier to date
It measures an asteroid's surface color

text: Which strategy changes an asteroid's orbit by transferring momentum without striking it?
What is the main purpose of an asteroid kinetic impactor mission?
choices: To measurably change an asteroid's velocity
To collect every meteorite it produces
To create a global crater network

text: Why is an asteroid's internal structure important for kinetic-impact deflection?
choices: Porosity and rubble-pile structure affect momentum transfer
It determines the asteroid's apparent color only
It fixes the impact date precisely

text: What is a rubble-pile asteroid?
choices: A gravitationally bound aggregate of fragments and void space
A monolithic crystal of pure nickel
A comet made only of ice
A crater filled with loose terrestrial soil

text: Which observation best constrains an asteroid's bulk density?
choices: Its mass combined with a volume estimate
Its visible brightness on one night
The number of craters on Earth

text: What is a hypervelocity impact?
choices: A collision at speeds high enough for strong shock and rapid vaporization
A low-speed collision between drifting boulders
A meteorite fall observed by radar
A crater formed only by volcanism

text: Which signature can indicate impact vapor condensation in a sediment layer?
choices: Fresh river pebbles with rounded edges
A layer of ordinary beach sand

text: What is a pseudotachylite in an impact setting?
choices: A frictional or shock-generated melt rock along faults
A primary mineral in carbonaceous chondrites
A weathering rind on an iron meteorite

text: Why can impact-generated melt sheets be valuable for geochronology?
choices: They may crystallize rapidly and record the impact event
They never exchange elements with surroundings
They form only before planetary accretion

text: What is an impact breccia?
choices: A rock made of broken fragments assembled or lithified by impact processes
A meteorite composed only of metal
A sediment formed solely by wind

text: Which evidence most strongly distinguishes an impact breccia from ordinary fault breccia?
choices: Coexisting shock metamorphism and impact melt features
A high concentration of clay alone

text: Why do impact simulations use equations of state?
choices: To model material behavior under extreme pressure and temperature
To classify meteorites by museum shelf
To calculate a meteor shower's radiant by eyesight
To identify minerals from color alone

text: What is a parent body in meteorite science?
choices: The asteroid or planet from which a meteorite originated
The field station that collected a specimen

text: What is an impactor?
choices: The body that strikes a target during a collision
The material deposited by a river
The uplift at a crater center

text: Why can asteroid spectral observations aid meteorite interpretation?
choices: They compare remote surface minerals with laboratory samples
They directly reveal an asteroid's exact age
They measure crater depth without images

text: What is a differentiated asteroid?
choices: One separated into compositional layers through melting
One made entirely of primitive dust
One that has never experienced impacts
One composed solely of water ice

text: Which process can create metallic cores inside differentiated planetesimals?
choices: Wind sorting on an asteroid surface

text: What does shock pressure estimate in an impact study?
choices: The peak pressure experienced by shocked material
The atmospheric pressure at a fall site
The pressure inside a museum case
The pressure of a comet's tail

text: Why are impact experiments performed with gas guns?
choices: They reproduce controlled high-speed collisions in the laboratory
They measure meteorite radioactivity without samples
They create natural craters on planets
They determine an asteroid's orbit directly

text: What is atmospheric ablation?
choices: Loss and heating of a meteoroid's surface during entry
Cooling of impact melt beneath a crater

text: Why can a meteoroid fragment during atmospheric entry?
choices: Aerodynamic pressure exceeds the strength of its structure
Its minerals all vaporize before contact
Its crater ejecta pulls it apart

text: What is a strewn field?
choices: An area where fragments from one fall are distributed
A ring of peaks inside a crater
A zone of impact melt beneath bedrock

text: What can meteorite pairing correct for in collection statistics?
choices: Multiple fragments from one fall being counted as separate stones
Errors in the meteorite's mineral formula

text: Why are contamination controls crucial in returned asteroid samples?
choices: Terrestrial material can obscure indigenous organic or isotopic signals
It prevents samples from forming chondrules

text: What is a cosmogenic nuclide?
choices: An isotope produced by cosmic-ray interactions
A mineral formed only in volcanoes
A gas released by terrestrial plants
An isotope created by ocean tides

text: What does noble-gas retention reveal about a meteorite?
choices: Its thermal history and possible loss events
Its exact impact angle on Earth
The color of its fusion crust
The number of craters on its parent body

text: What is a transient crater?
choices: The short-lived cavity formed immediately after impact
A crater filled by an ancient ocean
A depression made by wind erosion

text: What does crater excavation expose?
choices: Deep target rocks displaced upward and outward
Fresh cometary ice in every case
A layer of modern soil beneath the rim

text: Which measurement helps constrain the age of an impact melt?
choices: A radiometric clock reset or crystallized during melting

text: What is impact-induced hydrothermal alteration?
choices: Chemical change driven by hot fluids after an impact
Melting caused by sunlight on a meteorite
Sorting of grains by atmospheric wind

text: Why can impact structures host hydrothermal mineral deposits?
choices: Fractures and heat allow fluids to circulate through permeable rock
Crater rims always contain pure metal
Ejecta are made entirely of salt

text: What is the purpose of a meteorite classification committee?
choices: To establish recognized names and classifications for specimens
To assign planetary defense launch windows
To determine a crater's erosion rate
